edits.prose: In Wonderland, Alice asks the Caterpillar whether becoming a chrysalis and then a butterfly will feel a little queer. "Not a bit," he says.[^v1-c2-carroll] The fellow demanding to know who she is has a fairly drastic change of his own coming. I want to follow what keeps unfolding through those changes.

edits.evidence: Alice asks about chrysalis and butterfly; the Caterpillar answers “Not a bit.”
edits.purpose: Continuity of a living process through changing form; entry into the existing ripple argument.
edits.category: C: author-authorized literary addition; no replacement of existing prose
edits.after: In Wonderland, Alice asks the Caterpillar whether becoming a chrysalis and then a butterfly will feel a little queer. "Not a bit," he says.[^v1-c2-carroll] The fellow demanding to know who she is has a fairly drastic change of his own coming. I want to follow what keeps unfolding through those changes.

edits.prose: When Wonderland's cards fly at Alice, she wakes to her sister brushing dead leaves from her face.[^v1-c3-carroll] Carroll leaves the dream and its surroundings touching at that little seam. A leaf doesn't arrive with a queen printed on it. The brain supplies rather a lot.
edits.definition: [^v1-c3-carroll]: Lewis Carroll, [*Alice's Adventures in Wonderland*, chapter XII, "Alice's Evidence"](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~rgs/alice-XII.html).
edits.evidence: The attacking pack is followed immediately by waking with her sister brushing fallen leaves from her face.
edits.purpose: Literary juxtaposition of dream and sensory surroundings, without claiming experimental proof or a causal explanation of the dream.
edits.category: C: author-authorized literary addition; no replacement of existing prose
edits.after: When Wonderland's cards fly at Alice, she wakes to her sister brushing dead leaves from her face.[^v1-c3-carroll] Carroll leaves the dream and its surroundings touching at that little seam. A leaf doesn't arrive with a queen printed on it. The brain supplies rather a lot.

edits.evidence: The Queen demands sentence before verdict; Alice objects.
edits.purpose: Self-confirming judgment and the later wager about who or what is allowed to correct the self.

edits.after: The Queen of Hearts wants the sentence before the verdict.[^v1-c4-carroll] A self defending itself can conduct the same proceedings without raising its voice. The more interesting problem is who gets to call a witness.

edits.prose: Carroll's bread-and-butterfly has wings of bread and butter, a sugar head, and a dietary requirement for weak tea with cream. If it cannot find that, it dies.[^v1-i1-carroll] A wonderfully short recipe. Keeping it going is another matter.
edits.definition: [^v1-i1-carroll]: Lewis Carroll, [*Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There*, chapter III, "Looking-Glass Insects"](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Through_the_Looking-Glass,_and_What_Alice_Found_There/Chapter_III).
edits.evidence: The Gnat describes bread-and-butter wings, crust body, sugar head, and the diet of weak tea with cream; failure to find food means death.
edits.purpose: Pattern description versus the conditions of continued existence; a light aside after the existing feedstock qualification.
edits.category: C: author-authorized literary addition; no replacement of existing prose
edits.after: Carroll's bread-and-butterfly has wings of bread and butter, a sugar head, and a dietary requirement for weak tea with cream. If it cannot find that, it dies.[^v1-i1-carroll] A wonderfully short recipe. Keeping it going is another matter.

edits.prose: Carroll gives Alice a landscape laid out as a chessboard and offers her a place as a pawn.[^v1-i2-carroll] The Othello learner gets only the moves; the board has to take shape inside. It has found the squares without ever being shown the lawn.
edits.definition: [^v1-i2-carroll]: Lewis Carroll, [*Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There*, chapter II, "The Garden of Live Flowers"](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Through_the_Looking-Glass,_and_What_Alice_Found_There/Chapter_II).
edits.evidence: Alice sees the brooks and hedges forming a chessboard; the Red Queen offers her the role of White Queen’s pawn.
edits.purpose: World representation learned from moves; the existing next paragraph explicitly keeps subjective experience as the unproved leap.
edits.category: C: author-authorized literary addition; no replacement of existing prose
edits.after: Carroll gives Alice a landscape laid out as a chessboard and offers her a place as a pawn.[^v1-i2-carroll] The Othello learner gets only the moves; the board has to take shape inside. It has found the squares without ever being shown the lawn.

edits.prose: The White Knight keeps rain out of his box by carrying it upside down. Alice points out that the open lid lets the contents fall out.[^v1-i3-carroll] I can imagine the specification: waterproof, fully inspectable, sandwiches optional.
edits.definition: [^v1-i3-carroll]: Lewis Carroll, [*Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There*, chapter VIII, "It's My Own Invention"](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Through_the_Looking-Glass,_and_What_Alice_Found_There/Chapter_VIII).
edits.evidence: The box is carried upside down to exclude rain; its open lid lets clothes and sandwiches escape. The imagined specification is new prose, not Carroll dialogue.
edits.purpose: Light engineering joke about a partial account of success, beside the distinction between inspection and explanation.
edits.category: C: author-authorized literary addition; no replacement of existing prose
edits.after: The White Knight keeps rain out of his box by carrying it upside down. Alice points out that the open lid lets the contents fall out.[^v1-i3-carroll] I can imagine the specification: waterproof, fully inspectable, sandwiches optional.

edits.evidence: The White Queen screams before the pin slips and says afterward that she has already done the screaming.
edits.purpose: Anticipation versus history and accountability; leaves the famous backwards-memory quotation for Interlude 33.
edits.category: C: author-authorized literary addition; no replacement of existing prose

edits.evidence: Tweedledum proposes fighting until six and then dinner; Tweedledee agrees. The crow interrupts before the battle.
edits.purpose: Agreement on procedure does not itself settle purpose or civic judgment. Does not claim they actually fight until six.

edits.after: Tweedledum and Tweedledee agree to fight until six and then have dinner.[^v1-i5-carroll] Consensus has done its job; civics has barely begun.

edits.prose: Humpty Dumpty makes words mean whatever he chooses, then explains that the question is who gets to be master.[^v1-i6-carroll] A promise that can change its meaning whenever convenient is Humpty Dumpty with an API.

edits.evidence: Humpty Dumpty asserts his authority to assign meanings and asks which is to be master.
edits.purpose: The executor must not control the meaning of its own obligations; carries the existing freeze-promises/thaw-procedure wager.
edits.category: C: author-authorized literary addition; no replacement of existing prose
